    Morphisms vanishing at one vertex (Lemma 4.2) #

    Let L : Kron → Rep D be a functor from Kronecker modules to representations of a finite quiver, sending short exact sequences to vertexwise short exact sequences, such that every vertex lies in the support of L(S₊) or of L(S₋). If φ : T → U is a morphism of D with T ∈ C and L(φ) vanishes at some vertex, then φ = 0.

    This is the part of Lemma 4.2 used in Proposition 4.4. Instead of the natural identifications L(T)(x) ≅ L(S₊)(x) ⊗ V we argue with the quotient T → (V, 0) and the subobject (0, W) → U: at a vertex in the support of L(S₊), a nonzero φ gives a map T → S₊ whose image under L is surjective there, and dually at a vertex in the support of L(S₋).
